data.exact_reserve_text: The tables below illustrate the development of the estimates of cumulative claims for the Syndicate on an underwriting year basis, illustrating how amounts booked have developed from one reporting period to the next. Due to RITC where the 2018 prior claims were ceded out to RiverStone, the claims table below only showing claims after underwriting year 2018. All tables are prepared on an undiscounted basis. To aid comparability, currency amounts have been converted using 2024 year end exchange rates.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Extinguishment of liabilities through the 2023 RiverStone contracts distorted claims incurred and reinsurance balances; a true-up during 2024 resulted in a charge to profit and loss.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased materially in 2024 compared with the opening position, with an aggregate adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 247.7m (around 14.5% of the opening gross reserves). The development arises from adverse movements concentrated in the 2020-2022 underwriting years, partially offset by a favourable movement on the 2019 year. The syndicate notes that the 2023 RiverStone reinsurance-to-close and quota share transactions distorted the 2023 comparatives and required a true-up in 2024. Drivers include large loss development, movements in reinsurance recoveries and claims cost/inflation dynamics.
raw_causal_phrases: The tables below illustrate the development of the estimates of cumulative claims for the Syndicate on an underwriting year basis, illustrating how amounts booked have developed from one reporting period to the next.
Due to RITC where the 2018 prior claims were ceded out to RiverStone, the claims table below only showing claims after underwriting year 2018.
Unpaid insurance claims reserves are estimated on an undiscounted basis.
The Syndicate is also exposed to catastrophe losses which may impact many risks in a single event.

At 31 December 2024, excess claims inflation not captured in the historical development is considered a reduced risk to the adequacy of reserves relative to last year, given developments in the economic and legislative environment.
The extinguishment of liabilities through the 2023 RiverStone contracts has distorted the claims incurred and the reinsurance balance components of the 2023 segmental analysis.
This true up process resulted in a GBP 27.1m charge in the profit and loss during the finalisation of the RITC and quota share arrangement.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (note 13 b) as no single explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' line was provided. The 2023 RiverStone RITC/quota-share transactions materially distort 2023 comparatives; triangle excludes 2018 and prior due to RITC. Amounts in the triangle are presented in GBP '000 and have been converted to millions. Where explicit gross PYD was not stated, triangle-based aggregation was used (confidence 0.8).
